clue.text: Casual wages of small gang

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a crew is a gang of workers

explanation.surface: The pay handed to a small band of casual labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British slang a person's screw is their pay or salary, so casual here marks the slang register.

clue.text: Shaping smart round vessel involving utmost of skill

indicators.note: round says the word for smart goes around the other letters

parts.note: to smart is to sting, as a cut does

indicators.note: involving says the vessel takes in a letter

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel

indicators.note: utmost of picks the furthest, final letter of skill

explanation.surface: Fashioning a stylish pot with great skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Carving or modelling a statue is a form of forming material into a figure, so the participle means forming.

clue.text: Broadcast publicity in Olympic city

indicators.note: in says the publicity sits inside the city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympic Games
an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: An advertisement transmitted in the Olympic host city.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting by wireless transmission of sound is what the medium does; the noun can name sound broadcasting.

clue.text: Such clothes are shabby, sadly outgrown, no good

indicators.note: sadly says the remaining letters are put in a sorry new arrangement
no says the letter for good is taken away

explanation.surface: Clothes a child has outgrown look shabby and are no use any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from OUTGROWN; 'sadly' rearranges OUTROWN. 'Such clothes are' introduces the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that has been used until threadbare and frayed is described as shabby.

clue.text: The umpire men finally chose thus

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is an umpire
OR, other ranks, stands for soldiers or men as opposed to officers

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word chose

explanation.surface: The umpire and the players at last made a choice, and so it was decided.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms meaning consequently or for that reason, introducing a conclusion.

clue.text: Number needing drink with supply principally lacking

indicators.note: lacking says that letter is missing from the word for needing drink

parts.note: thirsty means wanting a drink

indicators.note: principally takes the leading letter of supply

explanation.surface: Someone desperate for a drink when the supplies have dried up.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times ten is a cardinal figure, so it fits as a number.

clue.text: Pentagon's way to the top, no need to take flight?

definitions.text: Pentagon's way to the top, no need to take flight?

parts.words: Pentagon's way to the top, no need to take flight?
parts.note: the Pentagon is the US defence headquarters, so this is the American word for a lift; a flight is a staircase, which a lift lets you skip

explanation.surface: An ambitious officer climbing the ranks in Washington without running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take flight' looks like fleeing or flying, but a flight is a set of stairs. Pentagon signals American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a lift by this name: a cage raised and lowered between floors.

clue.text: Partly fear a chest pain in organ

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone half dreading a chest complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is the ear, and a pain there is a common childhood ailment.

clue.text: Company upset about boys hosting international events

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the company letters over

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: hosting says the boys take in a guest letter

parts.note: sons are boys

explanation.surface: A firm in turmoil over its boys staging international fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: Special happenings or functions, such as a wedding, are called by this word.

clue.text: Relieved and satisfied to be losing place

indicators.note: to be losing says a short abbreviation drops out of the word for satisfied

parts.note: pleased means satisfied
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A competitor glad to finish but disappointed to lose their position.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain or pressure that has been lessened or alleviated is a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Legend of row after two European articles

indicators.note: after says the row comes behind the two articles in the answer

parts.note: UN is a French indefinite article and DER a German definite article
a line is a row, as of people or trees

explanation.surface: A story about a quarrel told after a pair of foreign grammar words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legend' is the caption printed beneath a picture, not a myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a caption, the text placed beneath an illustration; the answer names such a caption in the sense of a line written below.

clue.text: Overstrains joints

definitions.meaning: to rack is to strain something violently
a rack of lamb is a joint of meat, so the plural gives joints

explanation.surface: Someone who overdoes exercise and hurts their joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Torturing on the rack meant stretching beyond bearing; separately, butchers sell rib cuts called racks of lamb.

clue.text: Racing driver securing victory over administrator

indicators.note: securing says the racing driver holds the other letters inside him

parts.note: Alain Prost was a French Formula One world champion
V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A Formula One driver clinches a win in front of a race official.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A provost is the head of certain colleges or a Scottish mayor, someone who administers an institution or town.

clue.text: Defendant condemned with no right

indicators.note: with no says one letter is dropped from the word for condemned

parts.note: accursed means doomed or condemned

explanation.surface: A person on trial is found guilty and loses their rights.
explanation.definitionFit: The person charged in a criminal court is referred to as the defendant or the prisoner at the bar.

clue.text: Provoke to action fashionable name

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
to cite is to name or mention, as a source or witness

explanation.surface: A trendy name is used to spur people into action.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or urge someone on to do something is a direct synonym of the definition phrase.

clue.text: A rest cure arranged for dependants

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of A rest cure are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A spa break booked for the people one looks after.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature in the old sense is someone who owes their position to a patron, a hanger-on or minion.

clue.text: No wonder decor was regularly constructed with this?

definitions.text: No wonder decor was regularly constructed with this?

indicators.note: constructed says the chosen letters are built into a new order
regularly takes every second letter of the run No wonder decor was

explanation.surface: Unsurprisingly, the fine interior was made from this prized timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the even letters OODREOWS from No wonder decor was; 'constructed' rearranges them, and the whole clue describes the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a dark, richly figured hardwood prized for fine furniture and decorative panelling, so lovely decor would follow.

clue.text: Criticised over salesperson turning up over a wide area?

indicators.note: over says the word for criticised covers the other letters

parts.note: dissed is slang for criticised or disrespected

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue reads the salesperson's letters upwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesperson

explanation.surface: Someone sniping at a sales rep who has just arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered or spread out across a large region; the participle of distributing widely.

clue.text: Strength consuming body of India rising in its hour of independence

indicators.note: consuming says the word for strength swallows other letters

parts.note: might means strength or power

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads those inner letters upwards
body of takes the inner letters of India, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: India's might growing in the hour it gained freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the inner letters of India upwards in this down clue. Nehru's famous speech marked independence at the stroke of twelve on 15 August 1947.
explanation.definitionFit: India became independent at twelve o'clock at night, so that hour is its moment of freedom.

clue.text: Like rock singer, runs to leave and is dancing in front of clubs

indicators.note: in front of places the scrambled letters before the clubs symbol
dancing says the remaining letters with is jig about into a new order
to leave says that letter departs from the word singer

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A rock singer quits the stage and is seen dancing outside the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests music but means stone here; 'Like rock' is an adjective describing a banded metamorphic stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic stone, and the adjective describes anything made of or resembling that stone.

clue.text: Habitual doubter not in command concerning staff

indicators.note: not says the in-command letters are removed from the doubter

parts.note: a sceptic doubts habitually
IC stands for in charge or in command, as in 2IC
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A cynic, no longer in charge, has views on the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a rod carried as a symbol of royal authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial rod held by a monarch as an emblem of sovereignty is a kind of staff.

clue.text: Cares for sea creatures

definitions.meaning: to look after the sick or tend someone
nurse sharks, sometimes just called by the first word, are bottom-dwelling sharks

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after marine animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means tends or looks after; the nurse shark is a species of fish known by that name.

clue.text: Rather odd university student organisation unable from time to time

parts.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

indicators.note: from time to time takes every other letter of unable

explanation.surface: A university's student body that keeps failing seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is the UK's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the ordinary or a little strange is a close synonym.

clue.text: Very sorry abandoning outlandish graveyards for heavenly place

indicators.note: outlandish says the letters of graveyards are rearranged once those are removed
abandoning says those jumbled letters are left behind by graveyards

parts.note: the word very in a sorry, jumbled state gives its four letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A grim apology for leaving strange cemeteries for paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes the letters of VERY, scrambled as 'sorry' says, out of GRAVEYARDS; 'outlandish' rearranges GAARDS. Asgard is the home of the gods in Norse myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the realm of the gods ruled by Odin is a celestial dwelling, like a heaven.

clue.text: Design to gently stroke seabird

parts.note: to pat is to tap or stroke lightly with the hand
a tern is a slender gull-like seabird

explanation.surface: A plan to stroke a seabird gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A design such as a repeated decorative motif on fabric or wallpaper is a synonym.

clue.text: Effectiveness in revolutionary aircrew operations

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words aircrew operations

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: How efficient a revolutionary air force's missions are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the hidden letters in aircrew operations; 'revolutionary' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Force or capacity to produce an effect, as in the potency of a drug, is a synonym.

clue.text: South African custom for traditionally barbecued meat dish

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African
usage means custom or habitual practice

explanation.surface: The South African braai tradition of grilling meat.
explanation.walkthrough: South Africans traditionally barbecue boerewors, a coiled farmer's banger, at a braai.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages are the classic food grilled at a barbecue, a seasoned minced meat in a casing.

clue.text: Naughtily at it, caught in upper room

indicators.note: naughtily says the letters of at it misbehave into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A couple caught up to mischief in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at it' is British slang for having sex, giving the surface its naughtiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A room just under the roof of a house, the top storey, is a garret or loft.

clue.text: Trashiest material journalist expunged

indicators.note: expunged says the journalist is struck out of the material

parts.note: worsted is a smooth woollen cloth
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: The most rubbishy copy gets struck out by the reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative meaning poorest in quality or most rubbishy describes the least good of all.

clue.text: Marks scale of French usage essentially in grids

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the word for grids

parts.note: grates are gratings or grids, as over a drain
du is French for of the

indicators.note: essentially picks out the central letter of the word usage

explanation.surface: A teacher grading the French usage in pupils' exercise grids.
explanation.definitionFit: To graduate a measuring instrument is to mark it with degrees or divisions, so the verb fits marking a scale.

clue.text: Admired 19 wandering with energy (and daughter)

indicators.note: wandering says the letters of that answer roam into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 19 down, a staff of royal office
E is the physics symbol for energy
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: the 19 answer, scrambled, with energy and a daughter added.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' stands for the answer to 19 down, whose letters 'wandering' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Held in high esteem or looked up to; a synonym in the past participle form.

clue.text: Thrashed youth outside church

indicators.note: outside says the youth wraps around the church

parts.note: a lad is a youth or young man
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A boy gets a beating just outside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace someone is old-fashioned slang for beating or whipping them, so the past form means beaten.
